attributes.body_ja:
五段動詞（ごだんどうし）「従（したが）う」のテ形（けい）「従（したが）って」が接続詞（せつぞくし）として使（つか）われると「(A) のため (B)」や「(A) の結果（けっか） (B)」のような意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。「従（したが）う」は「(A) の指示（しじ）や状況（じょうきょう）に合（あ）わせる」などの意味（いみ）を持（も）っていますが、この表現（ひょうげん）は (A) によって生（しょう）じる論理的（ろんりてき）な結果（けっか）を表（あらわ）す場合（ばあい）にだけ使（つか）われます。

「従（したが）って」を使（つか）う文（ぶん）では、前（まえ）の文（ぶん）で原因（げんいん）が述（の）べられ、その結果（けっか）が「従（したが）って」から始（はじ）まる次（つぎ）の文（ぶん）で述（の）べられる、という形（かたち）が多（おお）いです。

これはかなり硬（かた）い表現（ひょうげん）なので、正式（せいしき）なスピーチや文書（ぶんしょ）の中（なか）で目（め）にすることが多（おお）いでしょう。
attributes.body:
When used as a conjunction, the う-Verb 従（したが）う 'to comply' in its て-form will indicate that something is 'following on from (A), (B)', or 'as a result of (A), (B)'. As 従（したが）う highlights something that 'obeys with (A)', this construction will only be used to show a logical conclusion that is caused by (A).

A typical pattern where 従（したが）って will be seen, is two sentences in which the first expresses a cause, and the second begins with 従（したが）って and then lists the logical result.

This is a fairly formal grammar pattern, so is more likely to be encountered in more formal speech or writing.

Both express logical consequence, but the tone and register differ. ゆえに is a formal, written connector meaning ‘therefore’ that presents a reason–result relation in a stiff, explanatory style, as in 天候が悪化した。ゆえに計画を変更した (‘The weather worsened; therefore, we changed the plan.’). したがって also means ‘therefore’ but is more neutral and common in explanations or academic writing, focusing on logical progression rather than formality, as in 条件が満たされない。したがって実行できない (‘The conditions are not met; therefore, it cannot be carried out.’).

first_relatable.title: ゆえに
first_relatable.meaning: Because, The reason is, Due to, Therefore, So

attributes.body: Both したがって and から express a cause or reason. The difference is that から is common in casual, everyday speech, while したがって is more formal, used in writing or structured speech. Additionally, から appears in the middle of a sentence, while したがって comes at the start. To use から at the start, you would use ですから or だから.

まま(に) describes being left in a certain state, often implying lack of freedom or control, as in 言われるままに従った (I obeyed just as I was told). したがって is a formal connector meaning therefore or thus, used to show logical consequence, as in 天気は悪い。したがって中止する (The weather is bad. Therefore, it will be canceled).

first_relatable.title: まま(に)
first_relatable.meaning: As (one likes, feels or pleases), Spur of the moment, Wherever one fancies, Spontaneously, On a whim

attributes.body: その結果 and したがって are similar in that both express a result or consequence with a relatively formal tone. その結果 emphasizes the resulting situation or condition, similar to the English 'as a result of that', while したがって implies a logical conclusion, which may or may not necessarily be a 'resulting' situation.

そこで and したがって are both used at the beginning of a sentence to express one action following another, but differ in nuance and tone. そこで is a general-purpose expression usable in various situations and contexts, like the English 'so' or 'as such'. In contrast, したがって is more formal and has a stricter 'following from that' or 'thus' nuance.
